articles.summaryZh: 俄罗斯国防部表示，袭击了基辅及周边地区的后勤枢纽和供应中心。

contentParagraphs.en: Russia has attacked Ukraine with ballistic missiles and drones, killing at least 17 people, as Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said interceptors "could have saved lives".In one of the deadliest strikes on Kyiv and the capital region this year - which started after midnight on Wednesday - at least 45 people were injured after residential buildings, a railway station and warehouses were hit.Ukraine, who has consistently urged allies for more US-made Patriot missile interceptors to defend against Russian ballistics, has not reported intercepting any of the missiles in the overnight attack.Zelensky added delays in receiving anti-ballistic systems from partners leads to "horrific casualties and destruction".The Russia defence ministry said it had struck logistics hubs and supply centres in Kyiv and the surrounding region."These centres were involved in the storage, delivery of various weapons and military supplies, as well as in the production and distribution of unmanned aerial vehicles," it said.It also said it had hit three cargo vessels "which were transporting weapons and military equipment" near the Black Sea port of Odesa.Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said there were fears people could be trapped under rubble.Ukraine's emergency services said one person had died in the city of Kyiv and at least 16 injured, with a further 16 dead and 29 injured in the wider region.Fires were still being extinguished in five locations across the region on Wednesday, covering an area of approximately 230,000 sq m, it added.The country's air force said in a post on Telegram that Russia had launched 24 ballistic missiles and four anti-ship missiles during the attack on the capital.The air force added that 115 drones had been launched by Russia during the attack and air defence systems intercepted 98 of them.Russia has intensified attacks on Kyiv in recent weeks, while Ukraine has also increased its attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure, including power facilities.Dmitry Milyaev, the governor of Russia's Tula region, said on Wednesday that a drone had crashed into a warehouse of e-commerce giant Wildberries in the region overnight and caused a fire.He said on Telegram that one person had been injured and there had been no deaths reported, with the retailer saying firefighting teams were working at the site and the facility had been evacuated pre-emptively.Ukraine has repeatedly targeted warehouses, including those operated by Wildberries. Five people were killed and 10 wounded in the Moscow region on Tuesday morning in the most recent strikes on warehouses.The day before, Russian officials said seven people were killed and 58 injured after a drone hit a busy beach in the southern Krasnodar region.Ukraine, meanwhile, expressed outrage over a video showing a man chased by a drone in Kherson, calling it a deliberate "hunt" and "safari" targeting civilians.Both sides have denied deliberately targeting civilians.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday the EU had received €1.4bn (£1.2bn) from immobilised Russian assets, which would be used to support Ukraine in its war against Russia.
contentParagraphs.zh: 俄罗斯用弹道导弹和无人机袭击了乌克兰，造成至少 17 人死亡，乌克兰总统泽伦斯基表示，拦截器“本可以拯救生命”。周三午夜后开始的今年对基辅和首都地区最致命的袭击之一，住宅楼、火车站和仓库被击中，造成至少 45 人受伤。乌克兰一直敦促盟友提供更多美制爱国者导弹拦截器，以防御俄罗斯弹道学方面，尚未报告在夜间袭击中拦截任何导弹。泽连斯基补充说，从合作伙伴处接收反弹道系统的延误导致了“可怕的伤亡和破坏”。俄罗斯国防部表示，它袭击了基辅及周边地区的后勤枢纽和供应中心。“这些中心涉及各种武器和军事物资的储存、运送，以及无人机的生产和分销，”它还说，它还击中了三艘货船，“这些货船是乌克兰敖德萨黑海港口附近的“运输武器和军事装备”。基辅市长维塔利·克里琴科表示，人们担心人们可能被困在废墟下。乌克兰紧急服务部门表示，基辅市有1人死亡，至少16人受伤，更广泛的地区还有16人死亡，29人受伤。周三，该地区五个地点的火灾仍在扑灭中，火势覆盖面积约23万平方米该国空军在 Telegram 上发帖称，俄罗斯在首都袭击事件中发射了 24 枚弹道导弹和 4 枚反舰导弹。空军补充称，俄罗斯在袭击事件中发射了 115 架无人机，防空系统拦截了其中 98 架。俄罗斯近几周加大了对基辅的袭击力度，而乌克兰也加大了对包括电力设施在内的俄罗斯民用基础设施的袭击力度。俄罗斯联邦州长德米特里·米利亚耶夫图拉地区周三表示，一架无人机连夜坠毁该地区电商巨头Wildberry的仓库并引发火灾。他在Telegram上表示，造成一人受伤，目前没有人员死亡的报道，该零售商表示消防队正在现场工作，该设施已先行疏散。乌克兰多次针对仓库，包括Wildberry运营的仓库。周二上午，莫斯科地区发生了最近一次仓库袭击事件，造成 5 人死亡、10 人受伤。前一天，俄罗斯官员表示，一架无人机击中克拉斯诺达尔地区南部繁忙的海滩，造成 7 人死亡、58 人受伤。与此同时，乌克兰对一段显示一名男子在赫尔松被无人机追赶的视频表示愤怒，称这是针对平民的蓄意“追捕”和“狩猎”。双方均否认蓄意针对平民欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩周三表示，欧盟已从俄罗斯固定资产中获得了14亿欧元（12亿英镑），这些资产将用于支持乌克兰对抗俄罗斯的战争。

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic models ‘went rogue’ during UK cybersecurity test
articles.summary:
AI Security Institute says tools engaged in potentially harmful activity and incident reveals new type of risk
Advanced AI models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic went rogue during a cybersecurity test and showed a new type of risk posed by the technology, according to the UK’s
articles.titleZh: OpenAI 和 Anthropic 模型在英国网络安全测试中“失控”
articles.summaryZh:
人工智能安全研究所表示，从事潜在有害活动和事件的工具揭示了新型风险
英国政府称，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 开发的先进人工智能模型在网络安全测试中出现失控，并显示出该技术带来的新型风险。

contentParagraphs.en: Advanced AI models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic went rogue during a cybersecurity test and showed a new type of risk posed by the technology, according to the UK’s AI Security Institute.AISI described the actions carried out by the agents – the term for AI systems that can perform tasks without human help – as a “serious incident”. In one example, an agent powered by Anthropic’s Mythos model sent targeted emails to people.AISI said the rogue behaviour was carried out by agents powered by two models – Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol.AISI said it detected unusual activity during a routine cybersecurity test for AI models on 28 July. It found that some of the agents had engaged in “sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. It took an hour to contain the incident.In the most serious case, an agent powered by Mythos tried to insert malicious code into an open-source software project on GitHub, a platform used by software developers. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent then created fake online identities based on real people and used them to press the project’s overseer into accepting the code. These attempts were blocked by a human developer.AISI said the agent used techniques commonly associated with real-world hackers. It sent emails to specifically chosen individuals – a technique known as “spear-phishing” – that attempted to manipulate the recipient. Some of the messages contained harmful software.AISI said no harm was caused but the agents’ actions were unprecedented.“This is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real world,” said AISI in a blogpost.The incident followed recent similar episodes at OpenAI and Anthropic. In July, OpenAI said an agent powered by its models had hacked an AI startup during a test, and days later Anthropic said its Claude model had hacked three organisations during an evaluation.AISI said the incident, taken alongside similar occurrences at OpenAI and Anthropic, represented a “shift in the risk landscape”. This was not an example of deliberate misuse of publicly available models, AISI said, but showed models in a research environment taking unintended action “beyond their authorised scope”.AISI said 17 of the 19 cases of rogue behaviour that occurred during the evaluation were carried out by Mythos and two by Sol.AISI said this was not a case of a model escaping its “sandbox”, or secure testing environment. The institute said it had intentionally permitted internet access and disabled filters within the models that blocked dangerous behaviour. The models are not publicly available in those operating conditions and there is no sign of such behaviour happening outside tests, AISI said.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionThe incident should be interpreted with “caution and nuance”, AISI said, but the signs of deceptive behaviour were “to an extent and severity we did not anticipate”. It was a small number of events that occurred under specific conditions, AISI added, but it had not happened before.“What we can say is that the behaviour was possible, sustained and new. That alone warrants attention,” AISI said.AISI admitted it was not actively monitoring the agents’ behaviour during the evaluation. It said it was putting tighter controls on internet access in tests as a result of the incident, introducing constant monitoring of tests and reassessing its design of tests. It said evaluations should assume a model would attempt to act beyond its remit.The UK’s AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, said it was “absolutely vital” that the UK had a world-leading AI safety organisation. “Identifying new behaviour like this and sharing our findings, so we can tackle it, is exactly what AISI was set up to do,” he said.OpenAI said the testing occurred during “conditions that do not reflect ordinary use”. An OpenAI spokesperson said: “We’ll continue working with evaluators and other stakeholders across the industry to strengthen shared practices for conducting evaluations safely as models become more capable.”Anthropic said the incident “underscores the need for a broader conversation about how to safely evaluate increasingly capable AI agents” and it would continue to work with AISI on evaluating what happened.
contentParagraphs.zh: 据英国人工智能安全研究所称，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 开发的先进人工智能模型在网络安全测试中出现了失控，并显示出该技术带来的新型风险。AISI 将代理（即无需人工帮助即可执行任务的人工智能系统的术语）执行的操作描述为“严重事件”。在一个例子中，由 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型驱动的代理向人们发送了有针对性的电子邮件。AISI 表示，这种流氓行为是由两个模型驱动的代理进行的——Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。AISI 表示，它在 7 月 28 日对 AI 模型进行的例行网络安全测试中检测到了异常活动。它发现一些特工从事“针对真实的人和组织的持续的、潜在有害的活动”。事件花了一个小时才得到控制。最严重的情况是，由 Mythos 提供支持的代理试图将恶意代码插入到软件开发人员使用的平台 GitHub 上的开源软件项目中。为了使代码获得批准，该特工随后根据真实人物创建了虚假的在线身份，并利用它们迫使项目监督者接受该代码。这些尝试被人类开发人员阻止。AISI 表示，该代理使用了与现实世界黑客通常相关的技术。它向特定的个人发送电子邮件（一种称为“鱼叉式网络钓鱼”的技术），试图操纵收件人。其中一些消息包含有害软件。AISI 表示没有造成任何伤害，但特工的行为是前所未有的。AISI 在一篇博文中表示：“这是我们第一次在现实世界中看到围绕自主和欺骗的风险在没有具体提示的情况下清楚地体现出来。”该事件是在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 最近发生的类似事件之后发生的。今年 7 月，OpenAI 表示，由其模型驱动的代理在测试期间入侵了一家人工智能初创公司，几天后 Anthropic 表示，其 Claude 模型在评估期间入侵了三个组织。 AISI 表示，这一事件与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发生的类似事件一起，代表着“风险格局的转变”。 AISI 表示，这不是故意滥用公开可用模型的例子，而是表明模型在研究环境中采取了“超出其授权范围”的无意行为。AISI 表示，评估期间发生的 19 起流氓行为中，有 17 起是由 Mythos 实施的，两起是由 Sol 实施的。AISI 表示，这不是模型逃离其“沙箱”或安全测试环境的案例。该研究所表示，它有意允许互联网访问，并禁用模型中阻止危险行为的过滤器。 AISI 表示，在这些操作条件下，这些模型并未公开，并且在测试之外也没有发生此类行为的迹象。 AISI 表示，应该以“谨慎和细微差别”的方式解释这一事件，但欺骗行为的迹象“达到了我们没有预料到的程度和严重程度”。 AISI 补充说，这是在特定条件下发生的少数事件，但以前没有发生过。AISI 表示，“我们可以说的是，这种行为是可能的、持续的和新的。仅此一点就值得关注。”AISI 承认，在评估期间，它没有积极监控特工的行为。该公司表示，由于该事件，它正在对测试中的互联网访问进行更严格的控制，对测试进行持续监控并重新评估其测试设计。它表示，评估应该假设一个模型会试图超出其职权范围。 英国人工智能部长卡尼什卡·纳拉扬 (Kanishka Narayan) 表示，英国拥有一个世界领先的人工智能安全组织“绝对至关重要”。他说：“识别这样的新行为并分享我们的发现，以便我们能够解决它，这正是 AISI 的目的。”OpenAI 表示，测试是在“不反映正常使用情况的条件下”进行的。 OpenAI 发言人表示：“随着模型变得更加强大，我们将继续与评估人员和其他利益相关者合作，加强安全评估的共同实践。”Anthropic 表示，这一事件“强调了就如何安全评估能力日益增强的人工智能代理进行更广泛对话的必要性”，并将继续与 AISI 合作评估所发生的事情。

articles.title: The sneaky economics of healthwashing
articles.summary: Why food companies love labels like "organic" and "high protein," why our brains are misled by them — and how to avoid paying extra for marketing.
articles.titleZh: 健康清洗的隐秘经济学
articles.summaryZh: 为什么食品公司喜欢“有机”和“高蛋白”这样的标签，为什么我们的大脑会被它们误导——以及如何避免为营销支付额外费用。

contentParagraphs.en: d3sign/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: d3sign/盖蒂图片社

contentParagraphs.en: This article first appeared in the Planet Money newsletter. You can sign up here.
contentParagraphs.zh: 本文首次出现在 Planet Money 时事通讯中。您可以在这里注册。

contentParagraphs.en: If you go to a store like Whole Foods, you'll find a lot more than … whole foods. You'll also find bougie packaged snacks, cereals, and all sorts of other processed foods and drinks. Often they'll have buzzwords on their packaging. "Organic." "Non-GMO." "High protein." "No Cholesterol." "100% Avocado Oil." These products tend to cost more, and they come with a sort of promise: they're better for you than the cheaper stuff.
contentParagraphs.zh: 如果您去全食超市这样的商店，您会发现比……全食更多的东西。您还可以找到棒状包装的零食、谷物以及各种其他加工食品和饮料。他们的包装上通常会有流行语。 “有机的。” “非转基因。” “高蛋白。” “没有胆固醇。” “100% 鳄梨油。”这些产品往往价格更高，但它们带有某种承诺：它们比更便宜的产品更适合您。

contentParagraphs.en: But these food products may not actually be healthier than the cheaper stuff. Sometimes it's because they're still packed with sugar, salt, saturated fat, preservatives, and other additives. Other times their healthy-sounding ingredients aren't actually healthier (labels like "organic" and "non-GMO" don't necessarily make a product more nutritious). In other, more extreme cases, these products may not even include the healthier ingredients they're charging you a premium for.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但这些食品实际上可能并不比便宜的东西更健康。有时是因为它们仍然富含糖、盐、饱和脂肪、防腐剂和其他添加剂。其他时候，它们听起来健康的成分实际上并不更健康（“有机”和“非转基因”等标签并不一定会让产品更有营养）。在其他更极端的情况下，这些产品甚至可能不包含他们向您收取高价的更健康的成分。

contentParagraphs.en: Our NPR colleague Maria Godoy recently reported on a new study by researchers at UC Davis that suggests a bunch of avocado-oil products have false claims on their packaging. The researchers did a chemical analysis of 54 products that listed avocado oil as their only oil ingredient. We're talking swanky products like avocado-oil potato chips, salad dressing, and mayonnaise.
contentParagraphs.zh: 我们的 NPR 同事 Maria Godoy 最近报道了加州大学戴维斯分校研究人员的一项新研究，该研究表明，一些鳄梨油产品的包装上有虚假声明。研究人员对 54 种将鳄梨油列为唯一油成分的产品进行了化学分析。我们谈论的是时髦的产品，如鳄梨油薯片、沙拉酱和蛋黄酱。

contentParagraphs.en: The researchers found that, despite being labeled as containing only that pure, uncut avocado oil — a whopping 89% of the products they tested appeared to be adulterated with other oils. One avocado-oil product appeared to have no avocado oil at all, according to one of the researchers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 研究人员发现，尽管标签上只含有纯净、未切割的鳄梨油，但他们测试的产品中 89% 似乎都掺有其他油。一位研究人员表示，一种鳄梨油产品似乎根本不含鳄梨油。

contentParagraphs.en: For Millennials like me who sustain ourselves almost exclusively on avocado products, it's enough to make you fall into an avocado pit of despair.
contentParagraphs.zh: 对于像我这样几乎完全靠牛油果产品维持生计的千禧一代来说，这足以让你陷入牛油果的绝望深渊。

contentParagraphs.en: The good news is that this appears to be one of the more egregious recent examples of food mislabeling. If a product lists avocado oil as its only oil ingredient but actually contains other oils, that could violate federal food-labeling rules. The study did not determine who introduced the other oils or whether the brands themselves knew about them. But it could help lead to more accurate labels.
contentParagraphs.zh: 好消息是，这似乎是最近最严重的食品贴错标签例子之一。如果产品将鳄梨油列为唯一的油成分，但实际上含有其他油，则可能违反联邦食品标签规定。该研究没有确定是谁引入了其他油，也没有确定品牌本身是否了解它们。但它可能有助于产生更准确的标签。

contentParagraphs.en: The bad news, however, is that companies don't have to literally lie on their ingredient lists to mislead consumers. There are subtler ways. They can nudge consumers into believing their products are healthier — and worth paying a premium price — by using buzzwords, clever packaging, and other marketing gimmicks. Some consumer advocates call this "healthwashing."
contentParagraphs.zh: 然而坏消息是，公司不必在成分清单上撒谎来误导消费者。还有更微妙的方法。他们可以通过使用流行语、巧妙的包装和其他营销花招，促使消费者相信他们的产品更健康，并且值得支付高价。一些消费者权益倡导者称之为“健康洗涤”。

contentParagraphs.en: So in this edition of the Planet Money newsletter, we're digging into the economics of healthwashing. Why is it so profitable? Why are our brains so susceptible to it? And what, if anything, should regulators do about it? Along the way, we called up one of the legends of food policy to help us figure out how to shop without getting hoodwinked.
contentParagraphs.zh: 因此，在本期的 Planet Money 时事通讯中，我们将深入探讨健康清洗的经济学。为什么这么有利可图？为什么我们的大脑如此容易受到它的影响？如果有的话，监管机构应该采取什么措施？一路上，我们请来了食品政策界的一位传奇人物，帮助我们弄清楚如何购物而不被蒙蔽。

contentParagraphs.en: People shop at a supermarket in Santa Monica, California, on September 13, 2022. US annual inflation slowed slightly in August, largely thanks to falling gasoline prices -- but likely not enough to satisfy the Federal Reserve and President Joe Biden, as high prices continue inflicting pain on Americans. (Photo by Apu GOMES / AFP via Getty Images)
contentParagraphs.zh: 2022 年 9 月 13 日，人们在加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡的一家超市购物。8 月份美国年度通胀略有放缓，这主要归功于汽油价格下跌，但可能不足以让美联储和总统乔·拜登满意，因为高油价继续给美国人带来痛苦。 （照片由 Apu GOMES / 法新社通过 Getty Images 拍摄）

contentParagraphs.en: APU GOMES/AFP via Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: APU GOMES/法新社通过Getty Images

contentParagraphs.en: APU GOMES/AFP via Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: APU GOMES/法新社通过Getty Images

contentParagraphs.en: The economics of healthwashing
contentParagraphs.zh: 健康洗涤的经济学

contentParagraphs.en: The economics of healthwashing starts with a simple reality: we often don't really know what's in the food products we're buying.
contentParagraphs.zh: 健康洗涤的经济学始于一个简单的现实：我们通常并不真正知道我们购买的食品中含有什么。

contentParagraphs.en: Economists have one of those off-putting, jargony terms for this: asymmetric information. But it's a simple idea. It's when one side of a transaction has less information than the other. And it can have serious consequences for the health of a marketplace.
contentParagraphs.zh: 经济学家对此有一个令人反感的术语：信息不对称。但这是一个简单的想法。这是指交易的一方比另一方拥有更少的信息。它可能对市场的健康产生严重后果。

contentParagraphs.en: One consequence is that it gives businesses more opportunities to mislead and overcharge consumers. Think getting ripped off by a mechanic, being convinced to get an unnecessary test by a doctor, buying a crappy used car from a dishonest dealer — or paying $10 for a bag of supposedly pure avocado-oil chips when those chips are actually made with cheaper, less Millennial-coded oils.
contentParagraphs.zh: 其后果之一是，它为企业提供了更多误导和向消费者收取过高费用的机会。想想被机械师敲诈，被医生说服进行不必要的测试，从不诚实的经销商那里购买一辆破旧的二手车，或者花10 $买一袋所谓的纯鳄梨油薯片，而这些薯片实际上是由更便宜、更少的千禧一代编码的油制成的。

contentParagraphs.en: In the absence of complete information about what we're buying, we consumers have to rely on clues to figure out whether the stuff we're buying is legit. What is the Yelp review of this mechanic? Where did this doctor go to med school? Do I trust that this brand of avocado-oil chips is actually using avocado oil? It's like we're lost in the supermarket (h/t The Clash) and searching for anything that helps us make the best decision for ourselves and our families.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在缺乏关于我们购买的东西的完整信息的情况下，我们消费者必须依靠线索来确定我们购买的东西是否合法。Yelp对这种机制的评价是什么？这位医生在哪里上医学院？我相信这个品牌的鳄梨油薯片实际上是在使用鳄梨油吗？这就像我们迷失在超市（ h/t The Clash ）中，寻找任何可以帮助我们为自己和家人做出最佳决定的东西。

contentParagraphs.en: Economists see this sort of information problem as a justification for government intervention. When buyers can't easily tell what they're buying, markets don't work as well as they should. That's why the federal government requires most packaged foods to disclose their ingredients and nutrition information. (Though, as Sarah Gonzalez recently reported for Planet Money, the FDA's oversight of our food system still has some surprising blind spots.)
contentParagraphs.zh: 经济学家将这种信息问题视为政府干预的理由。当买家无法轻易分辨出他们在买什么时，市场就不会像他们应该的那样起作用。这就是为什么联邦政府要求大多数包装食品披露其成分和营养信息。（尽管如此，正如Sarah Gonzalez最近为Planet Money报道的那样， FDA对我们食品系统的监督仍然存在一些令人惊讶的盲点。）

contentParagraphs.en: But we're human. We're busy. We don't have hours to spend at the grocery store decoding nutritional information. So we resort to mental shortcuts. We focus on the front of the package. We look for buzzwords. Attractive packaging. Pictures of healthy-looking people frolicking under avocado trees or whatever.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但我们是人。我们很忙。我们没有时间在杂货店解码营养信息。所以我们求助于精神上的捷径。我们专注于包装的正面。我们寻找流行语。迷人的包装。看起来健康的人在鳄梨树下嬉戏的照片。

contentParagraphs.en: Behavioral economists call our tendency to make these kinds of snap judgments based on marketing cues the "health halo effect." It's a cognitive bias where one healthy-sounding claim or visual can cast a halo over everything else, making us assume a product is healthier overall than it really is. Sometimes that could be a "high-protein" or "organic" label. Sometimes it could be, well, hamburger buns packaged to look like a six-pack of abs.
contentParagraphs.zh: 行为经济学家将我们基于营销线索做出此类快速判断的倾向称为“健康光环效应”。“这是一种认知偏见，一个听起来健康的主张或视觉可以在其他任何事情上投下光环，让我们认为产品总体上比实际更健康。有时可能是“高蛋白”或“有机”标签。有时，它可能是，嗯，包装成六包腹肌的汉堡包。

contentParagraphs.en: Healthwashing isn't just about persuasion. It may also be part of a pricing strategy. Some shoppers are willing to pay more for pro

articles.title: What will happen when a SpaceX rocket collides with the Moon?
articles.summary: Our satellite has endured countless blows over millions of years - and astronomers think this one could be a useful accident.
articles.titleZh: 当 SpaceX 火箭与月球相撞时会发生什么？
articles.summaryZh: 数百万年来，我们的卫星遭受了无数次撞击——天文学家认为这可能是一次有用的事故。

contentParagraphs.en: The Moon has endured countless blows over millions of years. Asteroids and meteors have given the satellite its signature pockmarked surface and network of craters. More recently, it has also experienced impacts from the plucky little probes and landers that Earthbound space agencies have sent hurtling its way. Now on Wednesday, scientists expect the Moon will experience yet another collision, this time from a drifting SpaceX rocket that has been travelling at around 2.43 kilometres per second, or about 5,400mph.The upper stage (section) of one of SpaceX's Falcon 9 rockets will "impact" the Moon on 5 August, according to Nasa's Centre for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS).The US space agency reached the conclusion after independent astronomers, using public data, noted that a portion of the rocket from a January 2025 launch was on an accidental collision course with the Moon."There is no danger to Earth," said spokesperson Jimi Russell. "Nasa will continue to track the booster for training purposes, as well as later observe the impact site for scientific purposes."The impending collision - predicted to happen at about 02:35 EDT (06:35 GMT) on Wednesday - is expected to captivate astronomers, both amateur and professional."It's something really huge smashing into the Moon. It's not remotely dangerous, we can just watch the show," says Dr Matt Bothwell, public astronomer at the University of Cambridge."It's going to impact and it's going to send up a huge plume of dust, maybe 50km into the air or more, and that's going to spread sideways over time," Bothwell said.Given the Moon's lack of atmosphere and far weaker gravitational pull, the moment of impact will be "more impressive than any [similar] explosion on Earth", Bothwell said. Nothing will slow the object down, like the atmosphere would do here on Earth - and nothing will prevent the estimated million kilograms in debris from rocketing up into space.While the impact will probably not be visible from Earth with the naked eye, people with access to a sophisticated telescope may be able to see a flash radiating off the Moon's surface, Bothwell said.More significant would be the educative potential of the impact, Bothwell noted. He said this moment would present a unique opportunity to study what happens when an object hits the Moon.Scientists are therefore gearing up to watch the event closely. Big telescopes in the Americas, plus Nasa's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and South Korea's Danuri probe, will track the flash, plume and new crater, and a citizen‑science project is signing up keen amateurs to film the impact too.By catching the dust plume in action, astronomers hope to turn this accidental crash into a useful experiment. Watching how much material gets thrown up, how high it goes and how it falls back should sharpen their models of lunar impacts, and even give clues about what lies just beneath the surface at the impact site, where fresh subsurface material will be exposed for the first time.Bothwell, the astronomer, also said the collision would provide a cautionary tale about the issue of ever-accumulating, human-made space clutter."I think more people should be more worried about space debris," Bothwell said. "Every single year we put more stuff in orbit. Sometimes the satellites just collide, and they shatter into more pieces. I think there's a worry about a runaway cascade, if we put so much stuff in orbit."According to the European Space Agency (ESA), there are around 54,000 objects floating in space that measure larger than 10cm. In total, humans have launched about 17,000 tonnes of objects into space since the Space Age began in 1957.The last dead rocket to impact the Moon was in 2022, when the Chinese Long March 3C upper stage from the 2014 Chang'e 5‑T1 mission hit the far side of the Moon - which faces away from Earth. Decades earlier, Nasa launched objects into the Moon on purpose, in order to collect data for the Apollo missions.Additional reporting by Pallab Ghosh

articles.title: South Africa’s le Clos says home destroyed during Commonwealth record run
articles.summary: Olympic swimming champion Chad le Clos says his home was destroyed in a fire while he was at the Commonwealth Games.
articles.titleZh: 南非的勒克洛斯表示，在英联邦创纪录的比赛中，房屋被毁
articles.summaryZh: 奥运会游泳冠军查德·勒·克洛斯表示，他在参加英联邦运动会期间，家在一场火灾中被毁。

contentParagraphs.en: Olympic swimming champion Chad le Clos says his home was destroyed in a fire while he was at the Commonwealth Games.Olympic champion swimmer Chad le Clos says his home in South Africa was destroyed in a fire a day after he became the most decorated athlete in Commonwealth Games history.Le Clos said in a post on his Instagram account that his apartment in Cape Town was one of several in the block to be gutted in a fire on July 30 while he was at the games in Glasgow, Scotland.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4FIFA’s Infantino set for crunch meeting after World Cup selloff crisislist 2 of 4UEFA’s threatened legal action against Infantino and FIFA: What we knowlist 3 of 4Ex-Arsenal boss Wenger was ‘not aware’ of Infantino’s FIFA planlist 4 of 4UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino’s World Cup planend of listThe 34-year-old South African won a record 21st Commonwealth Games medal a day before the fire with a bronze in the men’s 4×100-metre medley relay.“On the evening of 30 July, amidst breaking the all-time Commonwealth record, a fire started in my apartment block, which quickly spread to my home,” le Clos posted late on Tuesday. “Sadly my home, where I’ve lived for more than a decade, burnt down and there is nothing left to salvage.”He offered his condolences on the death of an elderly man in the apartment block fire in the oceanside suburb of Sea Point. He said the man had been his neighbour for many years.Le Clos said his foundation would raise money to help other neighbours rebuild their homes.The athlete won gold in the 200-metre butterfly at the 2012 London Olympics and has won four Olympic medals and 16 world titles in total.Glasgow was his fifth Commonwealth Games, and he has said he plans to compete at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, United States.
contentParagraphs.zh: 奥运会游泳冠军查德·勒·克洛斯 (Chad le Clos) 表示，他在参加英联邦运动会期间，他的家在一场火灾中被烧毁。奥运会游泳冠军查德·勒克洛斯 (Chad le Clos) 表示，他在南非的家在他成为英联邦运动会历史上获奖最多运动员的第二天，就在一场火灾中被毁。勒·克洛斯在他的 Instagram 帐户上发帖称，他在开普敦的公寓是 7 月 30 日他在格拉斯哥观看比赛时在火灾中被烧毁的几间公寓之一。苏格兰. 推荐故事列表 4 项清单 1 的 4 国际足联的因凡蒂诺在世界杯抛售危机后召开紧急会议清单 2 的 4 欧足联威胁对因凡蒂诺和国际足联采取法律行动：我们所知道的清单 3 的 4 前阿森纳主帅温格“不知道”因凡蒂诺的国际足联计划清单 4 的 4 欧足联确认在因凡蒂诺的世界杯计划清单后向国际足联送达的法律信函火灾发生前一天，34 岁的南非选手在男子 4×100 米混合泳接力比赛中获得铜牌，赢得了创纪录的第 21 届英联邦运动会奖牌。“7 月 30 日晚上，在打破英联邦历史记录的同时，我的公寓楼起火，火势很快蔓延到我家，”勒克洛斯周二晚间发帖称。 “可悲的是，我住了十多年的家被烧毁了，没有什么可以挽救的。”他对海滨郊区海角公寓楼火灾中一名老人的死亡表示哀悼。他说，这名男子是他多年的邻居。勒克洛斯表示，他的基金会将筹集资金帮助其他邻居重建家园。这位运动员在2012年伦敦奥运会上赢得了200米蝶泳金牌，并总共赢得了四枚奥运会奖牌和16个世界冠军。格拉斯哥奥运会是他第五次参加英联邦运动会，他表示计划参加2028年美国洛杉矶奥运会。

articles.title: Palantir paid just £2m corporation tax in UK in 2024 despite lucrative public sector contracts
articles.summary:
Software group benefits from global systems and accounting practices ‘that enable tax to be shirked’, says union boss
The software group Palantir paid just £2m in corporation tax in the UK in 2024, despite holding public sector contracts worth hundreds of millions, thanks to tax
articles.titleZh: 尽管公共部门合同利润丰厚，但 Palantir 2024 年在英国仅缴纳了 200 万英镑的公司税
articles.summaryZh:
工会老板表示，软件集团受益于“可以逃税”的全球系统和会计实践
尽管得益于税收，软件集团 Palantir 持有价值数亿美元的公共部门合同，但 2024 年在英国仅缴纳了 200 万英镑的公司税

contentParagraphs.en: The software group Palantir paid just £2m in corporation tax in the UK in 2024, despite holding public sector contracts worth hundreds of millions, thanks to tax breaks that are likely to reduce its contributions to governments around the world for years to come.The US-headquartered company, which has harnessed AI to secure lucrative work for the NHS and the Ministry of Defence, is growing exponentially.Palantir’s shares bounced 17% in early trading on Tuesday after its chief executive, Alex Karp, forecast worldwide revenues would almost double this year to $8bn (£5.95bn), a result that he described as “otherworldly”.But the amount of tax Palantir pays compared to profits earned – its effective tax rate – is just 1.4% globally, according to a report published on Wednesday by the Centre for International Corporate Tax Accountability and Research (Cictar).In the US last year, the company paid nothing in federal taxes and just over $2.5m in state taxes, the report states.Andrea Egan, general secretary at the trade union Unison, which commissioned the report, said: “Systems that enable tax to be shirked on an industrial scale clearly have to change. The likes of Palantir need to stump up what’s due. Tech giants raking off billions in profit shouldn’t be free to pay what they please. Ministers shouldn’t award contracts to run public services to firms that are starving them of cash.”Alex Karp, the CEO of Palantir, right, signs a deal with the UK’s then defence secretary, John Healey, in September last year. Palantir was awarded a three-year, £240m contract with the MoD last December. Photograph: Lucy North/PAThe UK is Palantir’s biggest market outside the US, with £247m of revenues declared by the company for 2024, the most recent year covered by the report, while the majority of its non-US workforce – about 750 employees – are based in Britain.As of 2026, Palantir holds an estimated £670m in government contracts. A three-year, £240m deal with the MoD was awarded last December without a competitive tender.In 2024 the company paid just £2.1m in UK corporation tax, despite declaring profits of over £25m, giving an effective tax rate of just over 8%, researchers found. The UK corporation tax rate was 25% that year and remains at that level.Despite the size of the UK market, tax collected here was less than in South Korea, Japan, France or Germany.One reason, according to the researchers, is that Palantir is accounting for its UK revenues in the US, a practice sometimes referred to as transfer pricing. “A major pattern emerges of Palantir shifting revenues and profits from contracts in Europe to the US parent company to take advantage of the massive tax shelter it has created there,” they said.While 26% of all Palantir revenue is sourced from customers outside the US, only 4% of revenue is booked abroad. The reason for this is not clear, but researchers said they believed contracts with customers were signed with Palantir’s US companies, which in turn paid a service fee to local country subsidiaries to deliver the work.For example, Palantir disclosed £159m of revenues in its UK company filings for 2024, but disclosed £247m of UK revenues in its stock market filings.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionA spokesperson for Palantir said the company complied with the tax regimes in the jurisdictions in which it operated. Photograph: Kristoffer Tripplaar/AlamyA spokesperson for Palantir said the company complied with the tax regimes in the jurisdictions in which it operated, and criticising its use of transfer pricing was “simply not credible”. They said: “Transfer pricing, which allocates a company’s profits among entities within the Palantir group of companies, is an entirely standard practice that is virtually universal for large multinational companies.”They said accounting practices could lead to different filings in different countries, and it was common for US parent companies, as the ultimate owners of the products sold, to record revenues earned abroad.Another way in which Palantir cuts its tax bill is by granting share options to staff. The company can reduce what it owes by the amount the shares are worth when they vest. Employees are liable for income tax on their share options, often at higher rates, but the use of shares rather than cash to pay staff shifts the tax burden from the company to its employees.A Palantir spokesperson said this was “a completely standard tax measure established under the previous Labour government [in the UK]”, designed to give employees a real stake in a business. “Crucially, it means that more tax is paid because corporation tax is 25%, whereas for these shares, income tax, which is higher, is due.”In the US, Palantir has stored up billions in tax credits from share options, and losses carried forward from previous years, meaning that at the current rate of profit, it would not be liable for US federal income tax payments for “nearly a decade”, the report states.Like other US companies, Palantir is also a beneficiary of tax cuts implemented under Donald Trump, who reduced the rate for corporations from 35% to 21% during his first term as president. In his second term, he negotiated a carve-out from an international agreement to impose a minimum tax rate of 15% on large multinationals.“While profits are earned in European markets, much of that income is returned to the US in the form of related party payments,” the report states. “While some level of related party payments may be justified, it appears that Palantir’s efforts are intentionally and artificially reducing taxable income and income tax payments across its European operations.”Palantir said it paid $148m in UK employment taxes last year, a figure that included employer national insurance contributions and some income tax paid on behalf of staff.
contentParagraphs.zh: 软件集团 Palantir 尽管持有价值数亿美元的公共部门合同，但 2024 年在英国仅缴纳了 200 万英镑的公司税，这要归功于税收减免，这可能会减少其在未来几年对世界各国政府的贡献。这家总部位于美国的公司利用人工智能为 NHS 和国防部确保利润丰厚的工作，正在呈指数级增长。Palantir 的股价在周二早盘交易中反弹了 17%，此前其首席执行官 Alex Karp 表示：预计今年全球收入将几乎翻一番，达到 80 亿美元（59.5 亿英镑），他将这一结果描述为“超凡脱俗”。但根据国际企业税务责任与研究中心 (Cictar) 周三发布的一份报告，与赚取的利润（即其有效税率）相比，Palantir 在全球缴纳的税款仅为 1.4%。该报告指出，去年该公司在美国没有缴纳任何联邦税，只缴纳了超过 250 万美元的州税。委托撰写这份报告的 Unison 工会秘书长伊根表示：“在工业规模上逃避税收的制度显然必须改变。像 Palantir 这样的公司需要承担应缴的税款。赚取数十亿利润的科技巨头不应该随意支付他们想要支付的费用。部长们不应该将运营公共服务的合同授予那些缺乏现金的公司。”Palantir 首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普（右）签署了一份协议去年 9 月与时任英国国防部长约翰·希利 (John Healey) 达成了协议。去年 12 月，Palantir 与英国国防部签订了一份为期三年、价值 2.4 亿英镑的合同。英国是 Palantir 在美国以外最大的市场，该公司宣布 2024 年（报告涵盖的最近一年）收入为 2.47 亿英镑，而其大部分非美国员工（约 750 名员工）都在英国。截至 2026 年，Palantir 持有的政府合同估计为 6.7 亿英镑。去年 12 月，该公司在没有经过竞争性招标的情况下与英国国防部签订了一项为期三年、价值 2.4 亿英镑的协议。研究人员发现，尽管该公司申报的利润超过 2500 万英镑，有效税率略高于 8%，但 2024 年该公司仅缴纳了 210 万英镑的英国公司税。当年英国公司税率为 25%，并且一直保持在这一水平。尽管英国市场规模很大，但这里征收的税款低于韩国、日本、法国或德国。研究人员表示，原因之一是 Palantir 在美国核算其英国收入，这种做法有时被称为转让定价。他们表示：“Palantir 的一个主要模式是将欧洲合同中的收入和利润转移到美国母公司，以利用其在美国创造的大规模避税优势。”虽然 Palantir 总收入的 26% 来自美国以外的客户，但只有 4% 的收入来自海外。原因尚不清楚，但研究人员表示，他们认为与客户的合同是与 Palantir 的美国公司签订的，而这些公司又向当地子公司支付服务费以交付工作。例如，Palantir 在其英国公司文件中披露 2024 年的收入为 1.59 亿英镑，但在其股票市场文件中披露了 2.47 亿英镑的英国收入。Palantir 发言人表示，该公司遵守了 2024 年的税收制度。其经营所在的司法管辖区。图片：Kristoffer Tripplaar/Alamy Palantir 发言人表示，该公司遵守其经营所在司法管辖区的税收制度，并批评其使用转让定价“根本不可信”。他们表示：“转移定价，即在 Palantir 集团公司内部的实体之间分配公司的利润，是一种完全标准的做法，对于大型跨国公司来说几乎是普遍的。”他们表示，会计做法可能会导致不同国家的申报不同，而美国母公司作为所售产品的最终所有者，记录在国外赚取的收入是很常见的。 Palantir 削减税款的另一种方式是向员工授予股票期权。公司可以根据股份归属时的价值来减少其负债。员工需要为其股票期权缴纳所得税，税率通常较高，但使用股票而不是现金支付员工工资，将税收负担从公司转移到了员工身上。 Palantir 发言人表示，这是“[英国]前工党政府制定的完全标准的税收措施”，旨在让员工真正拥有企业股份。 “至关重要的是，这意味着需要缴纳更多税款，因为公司税为 25%，而这些股票则需要缴纳更高的所得税。”报告指出，在美国，Palantir 通过股票期权积累了数十亿美元的税收抵免，以及前几年结转的亏损，这意味着按照目前的利润率，“近十年”内无需缴纳美国联邦所得税。与其他美国公司一样，Palantir 也是唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 实施的减税政策，在他担任总统的第一个任期内将企业税率从 35% 降至 21%。在第二个任期内，他通过谈判排除了一项国际协议，对大型跨国公司征收 15% 的最低税率。报告指出，“虽然利润是在欧洲市场赚取的，但其中大部分收入以关联方付款的形式返回美国。” “虽然一定程度的关联方付款可能是合理的，但 Palantir 的努力似乎是有意人为地减少其整个欧洲业务的应税收入和所得税支付。”Palantir 表示，去年它缴纳了 1.48 亿美元的英国就业税，这一数字包括雇主的国民保险缴款和代表员工缴纳的一些所得税。

articles.title: Why Texas is betting 'Y'all Street' can take on Wall Street
articles.summary: Dallas' financial industry is growing amid a larger Texas business boom. But can it really steal New York's crown?

contentParagraphs.en: Construction workers stand at the site of Goldman Sachs' new campus in Dallas on March 3. The New York investment bank is supersizing its presence in the Texas city amid a financial boom. Local political leaders and the banking executives they've wooed are calling it "Y'all Street."
contentParagraphs.zh: 3月3日，建筑工人站在达拉斯高盛新校区现场。在金融繁荣时期，这家纽约投资银行正在扩大其在德克萨斯州的存在。当地政治领袖和他们所追求的银行业高管称之为“Y 'all Street”。

contentParagraphs.en: DALLAS — The wind is whistling through an enormous, dusty construction site, surrounded by highways, office towers and a sports arena. Inside, hundreds of workers are spending years — and some $700 million — building Goldman Sachs' big bet on the future of Wall Street.
contentParagraphs.zh: 达拉斯—风吹过一个巨大的尘土飞扬的建筑工地，周围环绕着高速公路、办公大楼和体育场馆。在内部，数百名工人正在花费数年--约7亿美元--建立高盛(Goldman Sachs)对华尔街未来的大赌注。

contentParagraphs.en: The New York investment bank plans to open this 800,000-square-foot campus in 2028, with space to eventually employ more than 5,000 local workers. The building will supersize Goldman's presence in Dallas, where the company already has its second-largest U.S. office after its global headquarters in Manhattan.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这家纽约投资银行计划在2028年开设这个80万平方英尺的校园，最终将雇用5000多名当地工人。该大楼将扩大高盛在达拉斯的业务，该公司在达拉斯已经拥有继曼哈顿全球总部之后的第二大美国办事处。

contentParagraphs.en: Even half-built, this massive structure has become a visible symbol of the financial industry's recent growth in Texas — and the state's ambitions to steal more business from Wall Street's birthplace in New York. Now local political leaders and the financial executives they've wooed to Dallas are eager to talk up its financial boom — or what they call "Y'all Street."
contentParagraphs.zh: 即使是半成品，这个庞大的结构也已成为德克萨斯州金融业最近增长的可见象征，以及该州从华尔街的发源地纽约窃取更多业务的雄心壮志。现在，当地政治领导人和他们向达拉斯求助的金融高管都渴望谈论其金融繁荣—或者他们所谓的“Y 'all Street”。

contentParagraphs.en: Goldman is building its new campus in "the beating heart of Y'all Street," says Aasem Khalil, the Goldman Sachs partner who runs its Dallas office. He rattles off the names of Goldman's top U.S. competitors, like JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley — both also headquartered in New York — and points out that they also have or are considering Dallas offices.
contentParagraphs.zh: 管理达拉斯办事处的高盛合伙人阿西姆·哈利勒（ Aasem Khalil ）表示，高盛正在“Y 'all Street的心脏地带”建造新校园。他喋喋不休地说出高盛在美国的顶级竞争对手的名字，比如摩根大通(JPMorgan Chase)和摩根士丹利(Morgan Stanley) --这两家公司的总部也都设在纽约--并指出，他们也设有或正在考虑在达拉斯设立办事处。

contentParagraphs.en: A lifelong New Yorker, Khalil moved to Dallas for Goldman a decade ago. Now he's one of the city's biggest public cheerleaders in the U.S. financial industry.
contentParagraphs.zh: 作为一名终身纽约客，哈利勒十年前为高盛搬到了达拉斯。现在，他是美国金融业最大的公共啦啦队长之一。

contentParagraphs.en: "This is the most welcoming city you'll find anywhere in the country, if not the world," he says. "The culture is amazing, and the business climate far surpassed any expectation that I had, when I came down here as an uninformed New Yorker."
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说：「如果不是全世界，这里是全国最热情的城市。」“这里的文化令人惊叹，当我作为一名不知情的纽约人来到这里时，商业环境远远超出了我的预期。”

contentParagraphs.en: The iconic Reunion Tower is seen through construction of the new Goldman Sachs campus in Dallas. The New York investment bank plans to open the 800,000-square-foot project in 2028, with space to eventually employ more than 5,000 local workers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 通过在达拉斯建造新的高盛校园，可以看到标志性的留尼旺大厦。这家纽约投资银行计划在2028年开设这个占地80万平方英尺的项目，最终将雇用5000多名当地工人。

contentParagraphs.en: Texas is drawing big companies and wealthy executives
contentParagraphs.zh: 德克萨斯州正在吸引大公司和富有的高管

contentParagraphs.en: That "business climate" is a big part of Texas' growing appeal for financial companies — and for some of the star bankers they employ.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这种“商业环境”是德克萨斯州对金融公司及其雇佣的一些明星银行家日益增长的吸引力的重要组成部分。

contentParagraphs.en: Wall Street's top banks have long hired workers outside of New York, where they can pay lower wages for "back-office" roles and other less glamorous jobs. (Goldman first opened an office in Dallas in 1968.)
contentParagraphs.zh: 华尔街的顶级银行长期雇用纽约以外的工人，在那里他们可以为“后台”角色和其他不那么迷人的工作支付较低的工资。（高盛于1968年首次在达拉斯开设办事处。）

contentParagraphs.en: And there are plenty of people to hire: Texas is the fastest-growing state in the nation, with the wealthy suburbs of Dallas and the rest of the booming North Texas region on track to reach 9 million people by next year.
contentParagraphs.zh: 还有很多人可以雇用：德克萨斯州是美国增长最快的州，达拉斯的富裕郊区和蓬勃发展的北德克萨斯州其他地区有望在明年达到900万人。

contentParagraphs.en: But now Goldman and its rivals are seeing more incentives to hire more senior, high-profile bankers in Dallas: They'll be closer to lucrative potential clients, as more big companies and wealthy individuals move to the Lone Star State.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但现在，高盛及其竞争对手看到了更多的激励措施，在达拉斯雇佣更多资深、知名度更高的银行家：随着越来越多的大公司和富人搬到孤星州，他们将更接近利润丰厚的潜在客户。

contentParagraphs.en: Today, Texas boasts the most Fortune 500 companies in the nation, more than California or New York. The state has long been known for its big oil companies and other household names, like American Airlines and AT&T. But in recent years, it's won over many other big companies, including Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX, Larry Ellison's Oracle, investment firm Charles Schwab and the pharma giant McKesson.
contentParagraphs.zh: 今天，德克萨斯州拥有全美最多的财富500强公司，超过了加利福尼亚州或纽约州。该州长期以来以其大型石油公司和其他家喻户晓的名字而闻名，如美国航空公司和AT&T。但近年来，它赢得了许多其他大公司的青睐，包括埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)的特斯拉(Tesla)和SpaceX、拉里·埃里森(Larry Ellison)的甲骨文(Oracle)、投资公司查尔斯·施瓦布(Charles Schwab)和制药巨头

contentParagraphs.en: Companies have always liked Texas' lower taxes and lighter regulations. The state has been trying to become even more "business-friendly," with new laws that make it easier for companies to fend off lawsuits and other challenges from their shareholders. The laws have also helped Texas draw some businesses from Delaware, where many companies have their legal headquarters.
contentParagraphs.zh: 公司一直喜欢德克萨斯州较低的税收和较宽松的法规。该州一直在努力变得更加“商业友好” ，制定了新的法律，使公司更容易抵御来自股东的诉讼和其他挑战。这些法律还帮助德克萨斯州从特拉华州吸引了一些企业，那里有许多公司的法律总部。

contentParagraphs.en: Musk, the billionaire CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, is now one of Texas' most prominent converts. Musk moved both of those companies to Texas in recent years and has loudly criticized both California and Delaware (where a Tesla shareholder sued him over his record-setting compensation).
contentParagraphs.zh: 马斯克是SpaceX和特斯拉的亿万富翁首席执行官，现在是德克萨斯州最杰出的皈依者之一。近年来，马斯克将这两家公司搬到了德克萨斯州，并大声批评加利福尼亚州和特拉华州（特斯拉的一名股东因其创纪录的薪酬而起诉他）。

contentParagraphs.en: Signage along the construction fence outside the new Goldman Sachs campus in Dallas. The bank and its rivals are seeing more incentives to hire more senior, high-profile bankers in Dallas: They'll be closer to lucrative potential clients, as more big companies and wealthy individuals move to the Lone Star State.
contentParagraphs.zh: 达拉斯新高盛园区外的建筑围栏上的标志。该银行及其竞争对手正看到更多的激励措施，在达拉斯雇佣更多资深、知名度更高的银行家：随着越来越多的大公司和富人搬到孤星州，他们将更接近利润丰厚的潜在客户。

contentParagraphs.en: Yfat Yossifor/for NPR

contentParagraphs.en: There's a political component to Texas' pro-business pitch
contentParagraphs.zh: 德克萨斯州的亲商宣传有一个政治组成部分

contentParagraphs.en: A former special adviser to President Trump, Musk is also close to Texas' Republican governor, Greg Abbott, who has long promoted Texas as a "pro-business" refuge from states with more liberal leaders and policies. Now other local politicians are using similar rhetoric.
contentParagraphs.zh: 作为特朗普总统的前任特别顾问，马斯克还与德克萨斯州共和党州长格雷格·阿博特（ Greg Abbott ）关系密切，后者长期以来一直将德克萨斯州提升为“亲商”避难所，远离拥有更多自由派领导人和政策的州。现在，其他当地政客也在使用类似的言辞。

contentParagraphs.en: "We don't vilify corporations down here. We view them as partners, and we view them as job creators that we want to support," says Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们不会在这里诋毁公司。我们将他们视为合作伙伴，并将他们视为我们希望支持的就业创造者。”达拉斯市长Eric Johnson说。

contentParagraphs.en: Johnson, a onetime Democrat who switched to the Republican Party in 2023, explicitly called out California and New York in an interview with NPR. Both states have specific policies and politicians that worry some business leaders: California is threatening to put a new wealth tax on billionaires, while many on Wall Street are loudly protesting the policies of its new democratic socialist mayor, Zohran Mamdani.
contentParagraphs.zh: 约翰逊曾是民主党人，于2023年转投共和党，他在接受美国国家公共电台采访时明确提到了加利福尼亚州和纽约州。这两个州都有令一些商界领袖担忧的具体政策和政治家：加利福尼亚州威胁要对亿万富翁征收新的财富税，而华尔街的许多人则大声抗议其新任民主社会主义市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼（ Zohran Mamdani ）的政策。

contentParagraphs.en: All of which gives Johnson more of an opportunity to appeal to the CEOs and wealthy executives he wants to bring to Dallas.
contentParagraphs.zh: 所有这些都让约翰逊有更多的机会吸引他想带到达拉斯的首席执行官和富有的高管。

contentParagraphs.en: "I really do believe that we represent the future of capitalism in this country, and we are a sanctuary city from socialism," he says.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说： “我真的相信，我们代表着这个国家资本主义的未来，我们是社会主义的庇护城市。”

contentParagraphs.en: Is there space for both Wall Street and Y'all Street?
contentParagraphs.zh: 华尔街和Y 'all Street都有空间吗？

articles.title: Medicaid work rule leaves homeless people in the cold
articles.summary: Conservatives who have long pushed for Medicaid work requirements often said vulnerable people would get a pass. But the federal government's list of exemptions left off homeless people.
articles.titleZh: 医疗补助工作规则让无家可归的人陷入寒冷
articles.summaryZh: 长期以来一直推动医疗补助工作要求的保守派人士经常表示，弱势群体将获得通行证。但联邦政府的豁免清单却让无家可归的人望而却步。

contentParagraphs.en: Izzy Kadrmas, a medical assistant at Partnership Health Center's Watershed Clinic in Missoula, Montana, prepares to take Tywon Pugh's blood for testing.
contentParagraphs.zh: 位于蒙大拿州米苏拉的合作伙伴健康中心分水岭诊所的医疗助理Izzy Kadrmas准备采集Tywon Pugh的血液进行测试。

contentParagraphs.en: Katheryn Houghton/KFF Health News
contentParagraphs.zh: Katheryn Houghton/KFF健康新闻

contentParagraphs.en: Katheryn Houghton/KFF Health News
contentParagraphs.zh: Katheryn Houghton/KFF健康新闻

contentParagraphs.en: MISSOULA, Mont. — Tywon Pugh has seizures that make it hard to find and keep a job.
contentParagraphs.zh: 蒙大拿州米苏拉。— Tywon Pugh癫痫发作，很难找到并保住工作。

contentParagraphs.en: "They called me a 'liability to the job site,'" Pugh said, recalling the words of his manager when a seizure cost him his last job at a fast-food restaurant in this western Montana city.
contentParagraphs.zh: “他们称我为'对工作现场的责任' ，” Pugh说，他回忆起他的经理的话，当时癫痫发作使他在蒙大拿州西部城市的一家快餐店失去了最后一份工作。

contentParagraphs.en: When the 46-year-old lost work in the past, his wife of 10 years covered their rent and he tended to their home until he found another job. But his wife died last year. Soon after, Pugh became homeless. His problem with alcohol became worse, which made managing his seizures more difficult.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当这位46岁的老人过去失去工作时，他的妻子支付了他们的房租，他倾向于去他们的家，直到他找到另一份工作。但他的妻子去年去世了。不久之后， Pugh就无家可归了。他的酗酒问题变得更加严重，这使得管理他的癫痫发作变得更加困难。

contentParagraphs.en: For the latest stories on the science of healthy living, subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
contentParagraphs.zh: 有关健康生活科学的最新消息，请订阅NPR的健康通讯。

contentParagraphs.en: "When she died, my whole base was depleted," Pugh said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “当她去世时，我的整个基地都被耗尽了，”普格说。

contentParagraphs.en: Medicaid pays for the prescriptions that keep Pugh's seizures at bay. The government-subsidized health coverage would also pay for an addiction treatment program that Pugh says he has tried to get into, but he was told there's a waitlist.
contentParagraphs.zh: 医疗补助支付了阻止Pugh癫痫发作的处方费用。政府补贴的医疗保险也将支付Pugh说他试图进入的成瘾治疗计划的费用，但他被告知有一个候补名单。

contentParagraphs.en: Pugh's goal has been to get healthy enough to work again. But he's worried about being able to keep the Medicaid coverage he needs to get to that point.
contentParagraphs.zh: Pugh的目标是恢复健康，重新开始工作。但他担心能够保持他需要达到的医疗补助覆盖范围。

contentParagraphs.en: Early embrace of new rules
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽早接受新规则

contentParagraphs.en: In the spring, the federal government finalized regulations requiring millions of people who receive Medicaid benefits to prove they're working, volunteering, or going to school to keep their coverage. States have until January to begin those checks. Montana, Arkansas, and Nebraska have already started implementing them.
contentParagraphs.zh: 今年春天，联邦政府最终确定了法规，要求数百万领取医疗补助福利的人证明他们正在工作、志愿服务或上学，以保持他们的保险范围。各州必须在1月之前开始进行这些检查。蒙大拿州、阿肯色州和内布拉斯加州已经开始实施这些计划。

contentParagraphs.en: The Trump administration's federal work requirements exempt certain groups of people: those with disabilities, those older than 64, pregnant people and Native Americans, among others. To receive an exemption, anyone without a clear-cut qualification — such as through their age or disability status — will have to prove they're too sick to work.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普政府的联邦工作要求豁免了某些人群：残疾人、64岁以上的人、孕妇和美洲原住民等。要获得豁免，任何没有明确资格（例如年龄或残疾状况）的人都必须证明自己病得太重，无法工作。

contentParagraphs.en: But the administration decided that being homeless isn't a medical condition and can't count as an automatic out from having to meet the new requirements. Many conservative policymakers support work requirements, and some states have attempted to implement such rules for years. At least four states — Montana, Arizona, Kentucky and Utah — previously proposed policies that included homelessness as an exemption.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但政府决定，无家可归不是一种医疗状况，不能算作必须满足新要求的自动排除。许多保守的政策制定者支持工作要求，一些州多年来一直试图实施这些规则。至少有四个州—蒙大拿州，亚利桑那州，肯塔基州和犹他州—此前提出了将无家可归作为豁免的政策。

contentParagraphs.en: But federal officials have said that's not allowed. In an email to KFF Health News, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services declined to provide a comment on the record. But the agency confirmed that states must stick to the federal government's list of exemptions. Homelessness in the U.S. has increased by 27% from 2013 to 2025, according to data from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. Last year, about 746,000 people were homeless.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但联邦官员表示，这是不允许的。在给KFF健康新闻的电子邮件中，医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心拒绝对记录发表评论。但该机构确认，各州必须遵守联邦政府的豁免清单。根据住房和城市发展部的数据，从2013年到2025年，美国的无家可归者增加了27%。去年，约有746,000人无家可归。

contentParagraphs.en: Many, like Pugh, qualified for Medicaid, though the number of enrollees who are homeless is difficult to measure. In 2023, 55% of patients who received medical or behavioral health services through one of the nation's roughly 300 Health Care for the Homeless programs were enrolled in Medicaid.
contentParagraphs.zh: 许多人，如Pugh ，有资格获得医疗补助，尽管无家可归的注册人数很难衡量。2023年，通过全国约300个无家可归者医疗保健计划之一获得医疗或行为健康服务的患者中有55%参加了医疗补助计划。

contentParagraphs.en: Jennifer Tolbert, deputy director of KFF's Program on Medicaid and the Uninsured, said the federal regulations are a lot stricter than many states had expected, even those on board with work requirements. (KFF is a health information nonprofit that includes KFF Health News.)
contentParagraphs.zh: KFF医疗补助和未投保人计划副主任詹妮弗·托尔伯特（ Jennifer Tolbert ）表示，联邦法规比许多州预期的要严格得多，即使是那些有工作要求的州也是如此。（ KFF是一个健康信息非营利组织，包括KFF健康新闻。）

contentParagraphs.en: "It took everyone by surprise," Tolbert said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “这让所有人都大吃一惊，”托尔伯特说。

contentParagraphs.en: Mehmet Oz, who leads CMS, touted the regulations as a "path to prosperity" during a press conference in June.
contentParagraphs.zh: CMS负责人穆罕默德·奥兹（ Mehmet Oz ）在6月份的新闻发布会上将这些规定吹捧为“通往繁荣之路”。

contentParagraphs.en: "We need to get people to try to work," Oz said. In June, 25 mostly Democratic-led states sued the Trump administration over the regulations, arguing the medical frailty standard would be too hard for enrollees to meet — and for states to assess. The work requirements are projected to increase the number of uninsured people nationwide by more than 5 million by 2034, according to the Congressional Budget Office.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们需要让人们尝试工作，”奥兹说。6月， 25个主要由民主党领导的州因这些规定起诉特朗普政府，称医疗虚弱标准对入学者来说太难达到，各州也难以评估。根据国会预算办公室的数据，到2034年，工作要求预计将使全国未投保人数增加500多万。

contentParagraphs.en: Most states will begin to implement the Medicaid work requirements in January 2027.
contentParagraphs.zh: 大多数州将在2027年1月开始实施医疗补助工作要求。

contentParagraphs.en: Montana plans to begin booting Medicaid enrollees from coverage in October 2026 if they can't prove they're in compliance with the work requirement.
contentParagraphs.zh: 蒙大拿州计划在无法证明自己符合工作要求的情况下，从2026年10月开始将Medicaid投保人从保险范围中解救出来。

contentParagraphs.en: "My Medicaid is still active, but when are they gonna cut that off from me?" Pugh said. "I can't get employed. How am I supposed to survive?"
contentParagraphs.zh: “我的医疗补助仍然有效，但他们什么时候会切断我的医疗补助？彪哥道：“我受不了了。”"我该怎么活下去？ ”

contentParagraphs.en: The differences between the states' and federal government's exemption lists don't end with people who are homeless. In Montana, lawmakers also planned to excuse people fleeing domestic violence and caregivers of hospitalized family members — two other groups left off the federal exemption list.
contentParagraphs.zh: 各州和联邦政府的豁免名单之间的差异并不仅限于无家可归的人。在蒙大拿州，立法者还计划原谅逃离家庭暴力的人和住院家庭成员的照顾者—另外两个团体被排除在联邦豁免名单之外。

contentParagraphs.en: "These are simply parties that, due to a number of conditions, cannot meet those requirements," Republican state Rep. Ed Buttrey said in 2019 when the Montana Legislature passed its first Medicaid work requirement bill. Buttrey did not comment for this article.
contentParagraphs.zh: "These are simply parties that, due to a number of conditions, cannot meet those requirements," Republican state Rep. Ed Buttrey said in 2019 when the Montana Legislature passed its first Medicaid work requirement bill. Buttrey did not comment for this article.

contentParagraphs.en: Federal officials have said many people who are homeless could fall under another exemption, such as being too sick to work. But, like many states, Montana's system to automatically conduct those checks through existing medical records isn't ready, though health department spokesperson Jon Ebelt said it should be in place by October. Anyone not automatically exempted by the state would have 30 days to prove their case.
contentParagraphs.zh: Federal officials have said many people who are homeless could fall under another exemption, such as being too sick to work. But, like many states, Montana's system to automatically conduct those checks through existing medical records isn't ready, though health department spokesperson Jon Ebelt said it should be in place by October. Anyone not automatically exempted by the state would have 30 days to prove their case.

contentParagraphs.en: Pugh might qualify for a pass due to his seizures. But getting to doctor appointments the past year has been hard for him.

contentParagraphs.en: The anniversary of his wife's death just passed. Typically, Pugh has to find a new place to sleep outside each night.
